source.section: Area Ratios Related to Side Length Ratios

subtopic: Area ratios and the angle bisector theorem

problem.text: In the diagram below, angle $ABC$ is a right angle. Point $D$ is on $\overline{BC}$, and $\overline{AD}$ bisects angle $CAB$. Points $E$ and $F$ are on $\overline{AB}$ and $\overline{AC}$, respectively, so that $AE = 3$ and $AF = 10$. Given that $EB = 9$ and $FC = 27$, find the integer closest to the area of quadrilateral $DCFG$.

steps.title: Where to start: find the whole triangle, then cut away the rest
steps.body:
Quadrilateral $DCFG$ is an odd shape, but everything else in triangle $ABC$ is made of triangles that share an angle or a height with $ABC$, so their areas come from length ratios. The clue is the right angle at $B$: it gives the full area. Then
$$[DCFG] = [ABC] - [ABD] - [AEF] + [AEG],$$
where we add back $[AEG]$ because that small triangle lies inside both $ABD$ and $AEF$.

steps.title: Triangle $AEF$ shares the angle at $A$
steps.body:
Triangles $AEF$ and $ABC$ have the same angle at $A$, so their area ratio is the product of the sides around that angle:
$$\frac{[AEF]}{[ABC]} = \frac{AE\cdot AF}{AB\cdot AC} = \frac{3\cdot 10}{12\cdot 37} = \frac{5}{74}.$$

steps.title: Triangle $ABD$ from the angle bisector theorem
steps.body: Since $AD$ bisects angle $A$, the angle bisector theorem gives $\frac{BD}{DC} = \frac{AB}{AC} = \frac{12}{37}$. Triangles $ABD$ and $ADC$ have the same height from $A$ to line $BC$, so their areas are in the same ratio $12:37$.

your_turn.prompt: Split $210$ in the ratio $12:37$ to find $[ABD]$.

steps.title: The overlap triangle $AEG$
steps.body: Inside triangle $AEF$, the segment $AG$ is part of the bisector of angle $A$. So the angle bisector theorem in triangle $AEF$ gives $\frac{EG}{GF} = \frac{AE}{AF} = \frac{3}{10}$. Triangles $AEG$ and $AGF$ share the height from $A$, so $[AEG]$ is $\frac{3}{13}$ of $[AEF]$.

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body: The part of triangle $ABC$ outside $DCFG$ has area $[ABD] + [AEF] - [AEG] = \frac{360}{7} + \frac{525}{37} - \frac{1575}{481} = \frac{209910}{3367} \approx 62.34$. So $[DCFG] = 210 - \frac{209910}{3367} \approx 147.66$, and the closest integer is $148$. The answer is **$148$**.
